newsitem.title: UK: Beacon Gas names managing director.
newsitem.headline: Beacon Gas names managing director.

text.p: Beacon Gas, the new Amoco Corp/Seeboard Plc domestic gas marketing and sales company, announced on Monday that Alan Lias, formerly of AGAS, will be the company's managing director.
Beacon is one of 11 companies so far licensed by U.K. industry regulator Ofgas to supply gas to domestic households in Britain's first two pilot areas.

The first area, opened for competition on April 29, covers the counties of Devon, Somerset and Cornwall. The second area is to be split into two sections, with Dorset and the former county of Avon opening on February 10 while Kent and East and West Sussex open for competition on March 7.
Beacon was launched on October 7, and a spokesman said on Monday that the company has started signing up customers although it will not supply its first gas until the second pilot area starts up.

The company is offering gas at a fixed price of 1.36 pence per kiloWatt hour (p/kWh), compared to the British Gas rate of 1.52 p/kWh. Beacon also offers lower standing charges, and estimates a typical customer will save 50 stg a year by moving across from British Gas.

Companies so far licensed by Ofgas to supply the domestic market in the first two pilot areas are: Amerada Hess Gas (Domestic) Ltd; Beacon Gas Ltd; British Fuels Gas Ltd; British Gas Trading Ltd; Eastern Natural Gas (Retail) Ltd; London Total Energy Co Ltd; Northern Electric Plc; Norweb Gas Ltd; Southern Electric Gas Ltd; SWEB Gas; and Texaco and Calor Gas trading as Calortex.

Ofgas said it had received formal applications from Scottish Power to cover the whole country except for the first pilot area; from Midlands Gas for the first two pilot areas; and from Norweb to cover the whole country.
The rest of Britain will be opened to competition during 1998.
